social.instagram_caption:
A bruise where you injected tirzepatide?
Here's what the label counts:

💠 "Injection site reactions" is a group of terms (bruising, redness, itching, pain, rash and injection site reaction), not just bruises: 6–8% by dose vs 2% on placebo, in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes, treated up to 72 weeks.
💠 Rotate your site each week: same area, different spot each time (stomach, front of thighs, or back of upper arm with help).
💠 Spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever? Call your prescriber promptly. If it's spreading fast or you feel very unwell, get urgent medical care.
💠 Signs of a serious allergic reaction: swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat; problems breathing or swallowing; severe rash or itching; fainting or feeling dizzy; very rapid heartbeat. The Zepbound Medication Guide says to stop using it and get medical help right away if you have any of these.

Save this for your next shot day.

#tirzepatide

For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
The carousel is accurate and safe, so it passes. I found three minor wording and citation fixes.

What I checked:
- **Prescribing information (DailyMed, updated 16 Nov 2026, Revised 11/2026):** Table 1 lists injection site reactions at 2% on placebo, 6% at 5 mg and 8% at 10 and 15 mg. That matches "6–8% by dose vs 2%". The footnote d quote on slide 6 is word for word. The population (pooled Study 1 and Study 2, up to 72 weeks) is described in the channel's standard terms.
- **Medication Guide:** the allergy list on slide 5 matches the guide's symptoms in the same order, and the "stop using it and get medical help right away" wording is kept.
- **Pen instructions:** "Change (rotate) your injection site each week" is confirmed. So are "at least 2 inches from the belly button" and "another person should give the injection" for the back of the upper arm. The rotation quote has one punctuation difference from the original.

The infection-warning slide is the channel's own general guidance and correctly carries no source tag. The CTA has the exact don't-stop line and ends on the required disclaimer. There's no dosing, no switching advice and no body-shaming. The relative-vs-absolute framing is clear (6–8% vs 2%), and the myth/fact slide makes an honest point that the 6–8% covers a group of reaction terms, not just bruising.

I couldn't open the three Lilly PDFs directly because the fetch returned unreadable binary. I confirmed their content through DailyMed (prescribing information) and search excerpts quoting the Medication Guide and pen instructions, so the PDF links are listed on that basis.

issues.claim: “You may use the same area of your body, but be sure to choose a different injection site in that area.”
issues.problem: The quote isn't word for word. The pen instructions read "You may use the same area of your body but be sure to choose a different injection site in that area." with no comma after "body". Text inside quotation marks has to match the source exactly.
issues.fix: “You may use the same area of your body but be sure to choose a different injection site in that area.” (Zepbound single-dose pen IFU)

issues.claim: At least 2 inches from the belly button.
issues.problem: This is accurate, but the instructions say "You or another person can inject" for both the stomach and the thigh. The slide only says it for the thigh, so a muted viewer could think the stomach is self-injection only. Optional consistency fix.
issues.fix: At least 2 inches from the belly button. You or another person may inject.
